title: Sri Lanka among countries facing lower 10% US tariff under new forced labour policy
byline: Sri Lanka has been placed in the lower 10% tariff category under a new United States trade measure targeting imports linked to forced labour, according to the Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR).

title: CPA Australia Chief warns of ethical reckoning for accountants navigating automated financial systems
byline: Prof. Dale Pinto emphasises that human judgment and professional skepticism remain critical as artificial intelligence reshapes the global finance function

title: Sri Lanka targets US$300mn in cinnamon exports as Alba price hits record Rs. 7,500
byline: Sri Lanka is targeting US$ 300 million in cinnamon export earnings this year as farm gate prices for premium Alba-grade cinnamon climbed to a record Rs. 7,500 per kilogram amid growing global demand.

title: Tea exports fall in June despite stronger rupee earnings
byline: Tea export volumes declined for a second consecutive month in June, extending the industry’s weak first-half performance, although higher rupee-denominated export prices helped lift average earnings per

title: Sri Lanka seeks China aid for bamboo, forest management
byline: Environment Deputy Minister Anton Jayakody has called for international cooperation to tackle the global environmental crisis, saying no country can face environmental challenges alone.

title: Bangladesh president to resign as pressure grows over Hasina’s planned return
byline: Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin, ​a former ally of ousted premier Sheikh Hasina, will resign on Friday halfway through his term, his spokesperson told Reuters on Thursday, ‌days after Hasina said she was returning home from exile to surrender following a court conviction.

title: El Niño could alter weather patterns, bringing rains to some areas and dry spells to others
byline: El Niño could lead to significant changes in weather patterns, with some areas experiencing excessive rainfall while others could face dry conditions, Meteorology Department Director General Ajith Wijemannage warned.

title: 21 companies under CID probe over alleged $700 Million import scam
byline: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) yesterday informed Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama that investigations are underway to establish the involvement of 21 leading companies in a large-scale racket involving the illegal transfer of foreign currency out of Sri Lanka under the guise of importing goods, in violation of the Customs Ordinance.

title: CAA fines 23 private hospitals, labs Rs. 5.8m over expired medicines
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has filed cases against 23 private hospitals and medical laboratories across the country after islandwide raids uncovered the use and storage of expired medicines and diagnostic chemicals, overcharging for laboratory tests, and other practices that pose serious risks to public health.

title: Private bus drivers, conductors to receive ETF membership
byline: Private bus drivers and conductors will be brought under the Employees’ Trust Fund (ETF) scheme, marking a significant step toward extending social security benefits to employees engaged in non-government public transport services.

title: Ranil pushes for select committee to resolve 1.1 million pending court cases
byline: Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe said he had proposed setting up a select committee to find ways and means to get rid of the backlog of cases.

title: Lanka Premier League: Galle Gallants cruise to third win
byline: Galle Gallants bounced back in style to record their third victory of the Lanka Premier League T20 tournament with a comfortable 60-run win over Jaffna Kings in the tenth match played under floodlights at the Rangiri Dambulla Stadium yesterday.

title: Sri Lanka among countries facing 10% US tariff under new forced labour policy
byline: Sri Lanka has been placed in the lower 10% tariff category under a new United States trade measure targeting imports linked to forced labour, according to the Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR).

title: France orders evacuation of peninsula as hundreds flee wildfires by boat
byline: Authorities in France have ordered the evacuation of the entirety of the Cap Ferret peninsula (Lège-Cap Ferret) in the south-west of France, with hundreds of people escaping the area by boat.

title: Google rolls out new selfie video sign-in feature
byline: Google on July 23 launched a new selfie video sign-in feature, allowing users another option to log in to their accounts or recover them in case they are locked out due to forgotten passwords or lack of access to their preferred devices.

title: Commotion in Parliament following warrant issued on MP Archchuna
byline: A commotion flared up in Parliament after MP Ramanathan Archchuna claimed a warrant has been issued to arrest him for failing to attend courts today.

title: US says it will use frozen Iranian assets to fund damage to ships as strikes continue
byline: The US military says it has launched strikes on Iran for the 13th consecutive night, with Iranian state media saying four people have been killed and five injured.

title: Birthday party shooting victim dies
byline: A 39-year-old man who was critically injured in a shooting at a birthday party in Wattala has died after being admitted to the Colombo National Hospital, police said.

title: President’s timely intervention secures 10% US tariff rate, says Mahinda Samarasinghe
byline: Strong Bilateral relations between the United States and Sri Lanka, timely action and relevant directives on the part of the President, hard work and focused negotiations by the Sri Lankan delegation has resulted in the reduction of tariff rates to 10 percent, Sri Lankan Ambassador to the United States Mahinda Samarasinghe said.

title: Expired medicines: Are financial penalties alone an adequate deterrent? - Former envoy Kananathan
byline: Every day, thousands of Sri Lankans walk into hospitals and laboratories believing that every medicine they receive, every blood test conducted and every diagnosis made is governed by one principle: patient safety.

title: Debate on no-confidence motion on Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara underway
byline: The debate on the no confidence motion on Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara got underway in Parliament a short while ago.

title: Rs. 150 million worth assets earned from drug money freezed
byline: Police have freezed Rs. 150 million worth of assets said to have been illegally accumulated by two individuals in Dewanigoda, Rathgama.

title: How Abhijeet Dipke became the face of India’s first Gen Z protest movement
byline:
They were just six words posted on X in a moment of frustration:
’’What if all cockroaches come together?’’

title: Google rolls out new selfie video sign-in feature
byline: Google on July 23 launched a new selfie video sign-in feature, allowing users another option to log in to their accounts or recover them in case they are locked out due to forgotten passwords or lack of access to their preferred devices.

title: BASL rejects government MP’s claims, challenges MP to repeat allegations outside Parliament
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) today strongly rejected allegations made in Parliament by Government MP Asitha Niroshana Egoda Withanage against BASL President Rajeev Amarasuriya, describing the claims as “utterly false, baseless, and made with malicious intent.”

title: No visa fee change for Sri Lankan pilgrims, India clarifies
byline: The High Commission of India in Colombo has clarified that there has been no change in the visa fee policy for Sri Lankan pilgrims travelling to India, while announcing the reintroduction of the free (Gratis) visa facility for eligible pilgrimage groups.

title: Rear Admiral Buddhika Liyanagamage assumes duties as Eastern Naval Area Commander
byline: Rear Admiral Buddhika Liyanagamage formally assumed duties as the Commander of the Eastern Naval Area today (24), at the Eastern Naval Command Headquarters in Trincomalee.

title: 10 killed, including security personnel, in suicide bombing in Pakistan
byline: Islamist militants rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into ​a Pakistani security checkpoint, killing 15 people, including ‌12 soldiers, in northwest Pakistan, the military said on Friday, adding that 12 militants had been killed in retaliation.

title: Supermarket fined Rs. 500,000 for selling Nadu rice above controlled price
byline: A supermarket in Gampola has been fined Rs. 500,000 after pleading guilty to selling locally produced Nadu rice above the government-controlled maximum retail price.

title: Eight mangrove ecosystems in Puttalam to be declared Protected Reserves
byline: The Ministry of Environment has decided to designate eight mangrove ecosystems in the Puttalam District as new protected reserves this year.

title: Four arrested over shooting at Wattala birthday party
byline: Four suspects, including two women, have been arrested for allegedly aiding and abetting the fatal shooting that occurred in the Palliyawatta area of Kadirana, Wattala.

title: Spain declares national emergency over wildfires near Madrid and in Avila
byline: The Spanish government on Thursday night declared a national emergency after a series of wildfires threatened communities near Madrid and in the neighbouring ​province of Avila, forcing more than 10,000 people to evacuate as ‌firefighters struggled to contain the blazes.

title: No-confidence motion against Justice Minister defeated
byline: The no-confidence motion brought against Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara was defeated in Parliament by a majority of 116 votes, with 36 MPs voting in favour and 152 against.

title: A/L admission card amendments open online until Aug. 3
byline: The candidates sitting the 2026 G.C.E. Advanced Level (A/L) Examination can make amendments to their admission cards online until 12.00 midnight on August 3, stressing that the deadline will not be extended, the Examinations Department said.

title: Early optimism gives way to weaker close at the CSE
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) closed lower on Friday as early buying interest gave way to profit-taking in several index-heavy counters, pushing both benchmark indices into negative territory by the end of the session. While the market opened on a positive note with broad-based buying across counters, selling pressure intensified during the latter half of trading, erasing the morning’s gains.

title: New Chairman and members appointed to Delimitation Commission
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed M. K. Saman Sri Ratnayake as the new Chairman and a member of the Delimitation Commission.

title: Navy seizes over three tonnes of smuggled Kendu leaves off Chilaw
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy has seized approximately 3,135 kilograms of smuggled Kendu leaves along with three dinghies during a search operation conducted off Karukapane Beach in Chilaw today (24).

title: Ex-Southern Province Chief Secretary arrested over alleged Rs. 16.5M fraud
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has arrested Rannulu Chandrasiri de Zoysa, a former Chief Secretary of the Southern Province, over allegations of financial corruption and procurement irregularities.

title: Bangladesh’s President Shahabuddin, 76, resigns citing health concerns
byline: Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin, a former ally of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, has resigned citing serious health issues, his office said on Friday.

title: Sri Lanka explores house arrest to ease severe prison overcrowding
byline: The Government is considering introducing house arrest and other technology-based alternatives to imprisonment as part of broader legal reforms to address severe overcrowding in Sri Lanka’s prisons, said Justice and National Integration Minister Harshana Nanayakkara.

title: Klopp starts Germany reign by threatening to quit
byline: Jurgen Klopp started his reign as Germany’s head coach by threatening to quit if the media invades his family’s privacy.
